title: Verify Before You Trust: AI Output, Errors & Uncertainty
summary: Learn how to evaluate AI-generated output for errors, unsupported claims, missing context, and uncertainty before using it in workplace decisions or communication.
objectives: Recognize that AI-generated output can be plausible but incorrect.
Use appropriate sources or evidence to verify important AI-generated claims.
Identify when uncertainty or missing context should be disclosed.

vocab.def: Checking a claim, result, or output against an appropriate source, record, calculation, or qualified reviewer.
A statement presented as true without adequate evidence.
A condition in which available information does not support complete confidence in a conclusion.
The record, document, person, system, measurement, or other origin used to support information.

sections.heading: AI can sound confident and still be wrong
sections.body: AI-generated text may be fluent and professional even when facts are inaccurate, details are invented, context is missing, or a conclusion is unsupported.

sections.heading: Important claims should be checked
sections.body: The higher the consequence of a decision, the more important it is to verify the information using appropriate sources, records, policies, calculations, or qualified people.

sections.heading: Separate evidence from generated explanation
sections.body: An AI explanation is not automatically evidence. Workers should distinguish between what a tool generated and what can actually be supported by reliable workplace information.

sections.heading: Preserve uncertainty
sections.body: If information cannot be confirmed, do not rewrite uncertainty as certainty. State what is known, what is unverified, and what still requires review.

practice.prompt: An AI assistant gives you a confident statistic for a report but provides no reliable source. What should you do?
practice.answer: Verify the statistic using an appropriate authoritative or workplace-approved source before using it.

practice.prompt: An AI-generated summary leaves out an important exception contained in the original document. What does this show?
practice.answer: AI output should be checked against the underlying source when accuracy and completeness matter.

quiz.question: What is the strongest response to an important AI-generated claim?
options: Check the claim against an appropriate source before relying on it
Trust it if the wording sounds professional
Assume the tool checked it automatically
Use it as long as several people like the answer
quiz.answer: Check the claim against an appropriate source before relying on it

lab.objective: Review simulated AI outputs and mark which claims are supported, unsupported, incomplete, uncertain, or require additional verification.

reflectionPrompt: Why can a confident-sounding answer be especially risky when it has not been verified?
